prompt: A manager ends every week with 'good job, team'. Team members say they have no idea what they're doing well.
tells: they have no idea what they're doing well
why: Vague praise can't be repeated; name what worked.
trap: SBI is a full structure; the gap here is any specific praise.

prompt: A lead tells a writer: 'Putting the summary in the first line made that doc easy to act on. Do that every time.'
tells: 'Putting the summary in the first line made that doc easy to act on.
why: Specific praise tells people what to keep doing.
trap: The doc used bottom line first; the lead's move is the praise.

prompt: In the team channel, a manager thanks an engineer for writing the migration checklist that let three teams upgrade without a single rollback.
tells: writing the migration checklist that let three teams upgrade without a single rollback
why: Name the act and its result.
trap: No specific meeting or moment is set up; it's targeted thanks.

prompt: In an interview, a candidate says they recognize teammates by naming the exact thing done and why it mattered, not just 'great work'.
A new manager realizes all their feedback is corrective. They start noting one concrete thing each report did well each week and telling them.
tells: noting one concrete thing each report did well each week
why: Specific positive feedback matters as much as correction.
trap: It's not following up on feedback they received.

prompt: A director thanks a junior analyst: 'Your note flagging the duplicate rows stopped us from overstating revenue to the board.'
tells: stopped us from overstating revenue to the board
why: Say what they did and why it mattered.
trap: No situation-behavior-impact setup; it's sharp, specific thanks.
